value.question: orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured is PROVED, sealed, and its build was never charted. Does it owe its chain retroactively, or does it stand?
value.reading_it_owes: The chain is what authorizes a build, and an unauthorized build in proven-space is exactly Law 8's hollow. Cost of this reading, stated plainly so it is not chosen by accident: the only way to pay it is to author orient/survey/decompose KNOWING the answers, which produces a chain that is true about content and fiction about sequence — and once that is done for one voyage it is available to every future one as 'chart it afterwards'. That is the gate learning to accept its own bypass.
value.reading_it_stands: The gate did not ask, so nothing was smuggled past a question that was put. The build is real, its proofs are real, its watch is armed and its validation is sealed; what is missing is the preamble's LEARNING (the trees got no deposit), not the build's correctness. Cost of this reading: a voyage that skipped the preamble is indistinguishable at rest from one that ran it, forever.
value.what_CC_did_with_the_sibling_while_this_: Nothing that presumes either answer. `constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured` is in the identical position (code committed at fe71a6d, 16 proof teeth, validation sealed, WATCHME probe armed, ticket at TICKETME, no chain, no component history at all) and CC did NOT take route B to move it, and did NOT author it a retroactive chart. It stays where it is with the finding recorded on it.
value.why_it_is_yours_and_not_CC's: Both answers are defensible and they build different things. CC will not pick by which one costs less work — that is the disposition the 2026-08-14 rule forbids wearing a design argument's clothes.

value.a: A GATE THAT NEVER RAN AND A GATE THAT PASSED YOU LEAVE THE SAME RECORD. `entry_gate: null` covers both, plus 'exempt'. This is the part that makes the hole invisible rather than merely present, and it is separately fixable from the jurisdiction itself — worth noting because the jurisdiction fix alone would leave every past record still unreadable.

FOUR LEGITIMATE MID-PATH OPENINGS AND ONE SKIP LOOK IDENTICAL TO A GREP. The shape 'journal opens past BUILDME' is not the defect; it is the defect's silhouette. What separates them is the gate's existence at the time, which is a date comparison against a ticket — cheap, but it has to be drawn or the fix reds history.

THE HOLE WAS FOUND BY A BUILD STANDING AT THE OTHER EDGE. constrain's ticket sat at TICKETME, so the only crossing available was the guarded one, and it refused. Had that ticket sat one state further along — as its sibling's did — the same build would have sailed clean and nothing would have been found. The instrument here was luck, and that is the argument for gate (4)'s standing measurement.

THE TICKET ABOUT THE BUILDME GATES COULD NOT ITSELF CROSS BUILDME — and not for its own reason. Cast by hand 2026-08-14, it carried a bare WATCHME (a summons naming no object) and `sorted_berth: null`, so `buildme_rides_the_sorted` would have refused it at the very edge it is about, for a different missing field. Re-fired through /sorted 2026-08-17 (berth sorted-20260817T225912-eef4f0a63ede.json). The population, measured: all four hand casts of 2026-08-14 carry both gaps, because each was written by copying a sibling — which is how a missing field propagates rather than recurring.

THIS TICKET BUYS DETECTION WHERE THE BUILDME EDGE BUYS PREVENTION, and naming the difference is what stops a later reader from mistaking it for a claim that the hole is closed. Asking 'was this build charted?' at the PROVEME exit is the right EVENT — it is the first moment the system is told a build finished — and it is strictly later than the harm. The earlier alternative, forbidding a journal from opening mid-path, is a named WRONG INTENT because it reds four legitimate pre-gate histories to close one hole. So the trade is deliberate, not an oversight.
